A.subject: Physics
A.text: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of 4 moles of a rigid diatomic gas from 0°C to 50°C when no work is done is _________. (R is the universal gas constant)
A.sol_text: Since process is isochoric (no work done), Q = nCv∆T = n(5/2 R)∆T = 4(5/2 R)(50) = 500R

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A deuteron and an alpha particle having equal kinetic energy enter perpendicularly into a magnetic field. Let r_d and r_a be their respective radii of circular path. The value of r_d/r_a is equal to:
A.sol_text: The radius of circular path in a magnetic field is given by r = mv/(qB) = sqrt(2mK)/(qB), where K is kinetic energy. For deuteron: mass = 2m, charge = e. For alpha particle: mass = 4m, charge = 2e. Since both have equal kinetic energy K, r_d/r_a = (sqrt(2*2m*K)/e) / (sqrt(2*4m*K)/(2e)) = (sqrt(2*2m*K)/e) * (2e/sqrt(2*4m*K)) = (sqrt(4m) * 2) / (sqrt(8m)) = (2*sqrt(m)*2) / (2*sqrt(2m)) = 2*sqrt(m) / sqrt(2m) = 2/sqrt(2) = sqrt(2).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: If A and B are two vectors satisfying the relation A·B = |A×B|. Then the value of |A-B| will be:
A.sol_text: Given: A·B = |A×B|. We know A·B = |A||B|cos(theta) and |A×B| = |A||B|sin(theta). So |A||B|cos(theta) = |A||B|sin(theta), which gives tan(theta) = 1, so theta = 45°. Now |A-B|^2 = A^2 + B^2 - 2A·B = A^2 + B^2 - 2|A||B|cos(45°) = A^2 + B^2 - 2AB·(1/sqrt(2)) = A^2 + B^2 - sqrt(2)AB. Therefore |A-B| = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 - sqrt(2)AB)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Consider a mixture of gas molecule of types A, B and C having masses m_A < m_B < m_C. The ratio of their root mean square speeds at normal temperature and pressure is:
A.sol_text: Root mean square speed is given as v = sqrt(3RT/M). Since v is inversely proportional to sqrt(M), and m_A < m_B < m_C, we have u_A > u_B > u_C. Therefore, 1/u_A < 1/u_B < 1/u_C as the masses m_A < m_B < m_C.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A nucleus of mass M emits a gamma-ray photon of frequency ν. The loss of internal energy by the nucleus is: [Take 'c' as the speed of electromagnetic wave]
A.sol_text: Using conservation of linear momentum: Mv = h*ν/λ = h*ν/c, so v = h*ν/(Mc). Loss of internal energy equals gain in kinetic energy plus energy of gamma ray: (1/2)Mv^2 + hν = (1/2)M(hν/Mc)^2 + hν = hν[1 + hν/(2Mc^2)]

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A radioactive material decays by simultaneous emissions of two particles with half lives of 1400 years and 700 years respectively. What will be the time after which one third of the material remains? (Take ln 3 = 1.1)
A.sol_text: The equivalent half life for radioactive material decaying by simultaneous emissions is given by: 1/T = 1/t1 + 1/t2 = 1/700 + 1/1400 = 3/1400, so T = 1400/3 years. Using N = N0 * e^(-λt), for N = N0/3: 1/3 = e^(-λt), so λt = ln(3). Therefore t = ln(3)/λ = ln(3)/[ln(2)/T] = T * ln(3)/ln(2) = (1400/3) * (1.1/0.693) ≈ 740.74 years ≈ 740 years.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The value of current in the 6 ohm resistance is:
A.sol_text: Method-I: Using Kirchhoff's Law for loop DBAD: -140 + 20I + 6I = 0 => 10I + 3I = 70. Using Kirchhoff's Law for loop ACBBA: 5(I - I1) + 90 - 6I = 0 => -5I + 11I = 90. Adding equation (1) with twice equation (2): 25I1 = 250 => I1 = 10 A. Method-II: Using equivalent cell concept: VAB = (140/20 + 0/6 + 90/5) / (1/20 + 1/6 + 1/5) = (7 + 0 + 18) / (15 + 50 + 60)/300 = 25/(125/300) = 7500/125 = 60 Volt. Therefore I1 = 60/6 = 10 A.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The radiation corresponding to 3→2 transition of a hydrogen atom falls on a gold surface to generate photoelectrons. These electrons are passed through a magnetic field of 5×10^(-1) T. Assume that the radius of the largest circular path followed by these electrons is 7mm, the work function of the metal is: (Mass of electron = 9.1×10^(-31) kg)
A.sol_text: Step 1: Calculate energy of 3→2 transition using Rydberg formula. hv = 3.4 - 1.51 = 1.89 eV. Step 2: Electrons move in circular path in magnetic field with radius r = (sqrt(2mK))/(qB), where K is kinetic energy. Step 3: Rearranging for K: K = (q×B×r)^2×m/(2m) = (1.6×10^(-19))^2×(5×10^(-1))^2×(7×10^(-3))^2 / (2×9.1×10^(-31)) = 1.08 eV. Step 4: Apply photoelectric effect equation: φ = hv - K = 1.89 - 1.08 = 0.81 eV ≈ 0.82 eV

A.subject: Physics
A.text: For the circuit shown below, calculate the value of I1: (A) 0.15 A (B) .1 A (C) 25 mA (D) 0.05 A
A.sol_text: Using Kirchhoff's voltage law and current divider principle: I1 = V2/R2 = 50/2000 = 25 mA. From the circuit, I = (V1-V2)/R_eq = (100-50)/1000 = 50 mA. Since I1 + I2 = I and I2 = 50 mA - 25 mA = 25 mA, therefore I1 = 25 mA = 0.025 A

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The arm PQ of a rectangular conductor is moving from x = 0 to x = 2b outwards and then inwards from x = 2b to x = 0 as shown in the figure. A uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane is acting from x = 0 to x = b. Identify the graph the variation of different quantities with distance.
options: A - Flux, B - EMF, C - Power dissipated
A - EMF, B - Power dissipated, C - Flux
A - Power dissipated, B - Flux, C - EMF
A - Flux, B - Power dissipated, C - EMF
A.sol_text: When arm PQ moves from x = 0 to x = b, the flux (φ = ax) linked with loop increases, so induced emf e_m = -dφ/dt = -a(dx/dt) = -av is constant (non-zero). Power dissipated P = (e_m)^2/R is constant (non-zero). When moving from x = b to x = 2b, flux remains constant (φ = ab), so emf becomes zero and power dissipated is zero. When moving from x = 2b to x = b, flux decreases linearly, emf is again constant (non-zero) and power is constant (non-zero). When moving from x = b to x = 0, flux becomes zero, emf is zero, and power is zero. Graph A shows flux increasing then constant then constant then decreasing, Graph B shows power non-zero then zero then non-zero then zero, Graph C shows emf non-zero then zero then non-zero then zero. This corresponds to option (D).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Region I and II are separated by a spherical surface of radius 25 cm. An object is kept in region I at a distance of 40 cm from the surface. The distance of the image from the surface is:
A.sol_text: Using refraction at spherical surface formula: (mu_2/v) - (mu_1/u) = (mu_2 - mu_1)/R. Given: mu_1 = 1.25 (region I), mu_2 = 1.4 (region II), R = -25 cm (center on left), u = -40 cm (object distance). Substituting: (1.4/v) - (1.25/-40) = (1.4 - 1.25)/(-25). This gives (1.4/v) + 0.03125 = -0.006. Solving: (1.4/v) = -0.037125, therefore v = -37.58 cm. The image is 37.58 cm from the surface.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The normal reaction 'N' for a vehicle of 800 kg mass, negotiating a turn on a 30° banked road at maximum possible speed without skidding is ________ × 10^3 kg⋅m/s^2. [Given cos30° = 0.87, μ_s = 0.2]
A.sol_text: In the frame of vehicle, the vehicle is in equilibrium under pseudo force F_p = mv^2/R. Using force balance: N = mgcos30° + (mv^2/R)sin30° and friction f_s = (mv^2/R)cos30° - mgsin30°. Combining equations (1)cos30° - (2)sin30°: N(cos30° - μsin30°) = mg, therefore N = mg/(cos30° - μsin30°) = (800 × 10)/(0.87 - 0.2 × 0.5) = 8000/0.77 = 10.2 × 10^3 kg⋅m/s^2

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The entropy of any system is given by S = α*β*n*[μkR/Jβ + 3] Where α and β are the constants, μ, J, k and R are no. of moles, mechanical equivalent of heat, Boltzmann constant and gas constant respectively. [Take S = dQ/T]. Choose the incorrect option from the following:
options: S, β, k and μ R have the same dimensions.
α and k have the same dimensions.
S and α have different dimensions.
α and J have the same dimensions.
A.sol_text: From the given formula S = α*β*n*[μkR/Jβ + 3], we analyze dimensions. S has dimensions [ML^2T^(-2)K^(-1)]. For the equation to be dimensionally consistent: μkR/Jβ must be dimensionless. Since μ is in moles (dimensionless in this context), k is [ML^2T^(-2)K^(-1)], R is [ML^2T^(-2)K^(-1)], and J is dimensionless (mechanical equivalent), β must have dimensions [ML^2T^(-2)K^(-1)]. For S = α*β*n*[...], α must be dimensionless. Therefore: (A) is incorrect because μR has dimensions [ML^2T^(-2)K^(-1)] not matching S; (B) α is dimensionless while k is [ML^2T^(-2)K^(-1)] - different; (C) S is [ML^2T^(-2)K^(-1)] and α is dimensionless - different (correct); (D) α is dimensionless, J is dimensionless - same. Option (B) or (A) is incorrect.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A current of 5 A is passing through a non-linear magnesium wire of cross-section 0.04 m^2. At every point the direction of current density is at an angle of 60° with unit vector of area of cross-section. The magnitude of electric field at every point of the conductor is: (Resistivity of magnesium = 44 × 10^(-8) Ω m)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The value of tension in a long thin metal wire has been changed from T_i to T_f. The lengths of the metal wire at two different values of tension T_i and T_f are l_i and l_f respectively. The actual length of the metal wire is:
A.sol_text: Using the principle that tension varies linearly with position in a suspended wire and the relationship T_i / T_f = (l_i - l) / (l_f - l), where l is the actual length, we can solve: T_i * (l_f - l) = T_f * (l_i - l). Expanding: T_i * l_f - T_i * l = T_f * l_i - T_f * l. Rearranging: T_i * l_f - T_f * l_i = T_i * l - T_f * l = l(T_i - T_f). Therefore: l = (T_i * l_f - T_f * l_i) / (T_i - T_f)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: AC voltage V(t) = 20sin(wt) of frequency 50Hz is applied to a parallel plate capacitor. The separation between the plates is 2mm and the area is 1m^2. The amplitude of the oscillating displacement current for the applied AC voltage is _________. [Take epsilon_0 = 8.85 × 10^(-12) F/m]
A.sol_text: For a parallel plate capacitor with displacement current: C = epsilon_0 × A / d; omega = 2*pi*f = 2*pi*50; Voltage amplitude V_0 = 20V; Displacement current I_d = C × (dV/dt) = C × V_0 × omega = (epsilon_0 × A / d) × V_0 × 2*pi*f; I_d = (2 × 3.14 × 50 × 20 × 8.85 × 10^(-12)) / (2 × 10^(-3)) = 27.79 × 10^(-6) A = 27.79 µA

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A butterfly is flying with a velocity 4√2 m/s in North - East direction. Wind is slowly blowing at 1 m/s from North to South. The resultant displacement of the butterfly in 3 seconds is:
A.sol_text: Velocity of butterfly in North-East direction: v_bw = 4√2(cos(45°)i + sin(45°)j) = 4i + 4j m/s. Wind velocity from North to South: v_ws = 0i - j m/s. Resultant velocity: v_bj = v_bw + v_ws = (4i + 4j) + (0i - j) = 4i + 3j m/s. Speed of butterfly: |v_bj| = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 m/s. Displacement in 3 seconds: |displacement| = 5 × 3 = 15 m.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A certain charge Q is divided into parts q and (Q - q). How should the charges Q and q be divided so that q and (Q - q) placed at a certain distance apart experience maximum electrostatic repulsion?
A.sol_text: The electrostatic force between charges q and (Q-q) separated by distance r is F = q(Q-q)/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r^2). To find maximum force, take dF/dq and set it equal to zero: dF/dq = (Q-2q)/(4*pi*epsilon_0*r^2) = 0, which gives q = Q/2. This means the charge Q should be divided equally into two parts of Q/2 each to experience maximum repulsion.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A steel block of 10 kg rests on a horizontal floor as shown. When three iron cylinders are placed on it as shown, the block and cylinders go down with an acceleration 0.2 m/s^2. The normal reaction from the floor if mass of the iron cylinders are equal and of 20kg each, is _____ N. [Take g = 10 m/s^2 and μ_s = 0.2]
A.sol_text: Total mass = 10 + 3(20) = 70 kg. Using Newton's second law for the system moving downward with a = 0.2 m/s^2: Weight - Normal reaction = ma. 70(10) - N = 70(0.2). 700 - N = 14. N = 686 N

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A person whose mass is 100 kg travels from Earth to Mars in a spaceship. Neglect all other object in sky and take acceleration due to gravity on the surface of Earth and mars as 10 m/s^2 and 4 m/s^2 respectively. Identify from the below figures, the curve that fits best for the weight of the passenger as a function of time.
A.sol_text: Weight at Earth's surface: W_E = 100 × 10 = 1000 N. Weight at Mars's surface: W_M = 100 × 4 = 400 N. During travel in spaceship between Earth and Mars, there exists a neutral point N where the net gravitational field due to Earth and Mars is zero, making weight zero at that point. The weight decreases from 1000 N at Earth, passes through zero at neutral point N, and increases to 400 N at Mars. This behavior matches curve (a), which shows initial weight at 1000 N, decreases to zero at an intermediate point, then increases to 400 N.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: The amplitude of wave disturbance propagating in the positive x-direction is given by y = 1/(1+x^2) at time t=0 and y = 1/(1+(x-2)^2) at t=1s, where x and y are in metres. The shape of wave does not change during the propagation. The velocity of the wave will be _______ m/s.
B.sol_text: At t=0: y = 1/(1+x^2). At t=1s: y = 1/(1+(x-2)^2). The wave shape remains unchanged, meaning the disturbance pattern has shifted in the positive x-direction. Comparing the two equations, the argument (x-2) in the second equation indicates the wave has moved 2 meters in the positive x-direction in 1 second. Therefore, velocity v = distance/time = 2/1 = 2 m/s.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: In the reported figure, heat energy absorbed by a system in going through a cyclic process is _____ πJ.
B.sol_text: For a cyclic process, the heat absorbed equals the work done by the system (since ΔU = 0 for a complete cycle). The work done is the area enclosed by the P-V diagram. From the figure, the cycle appears to be rectangular with: Width = 40 - 20 = 20 litre Height = 40 - 10 = 30 kPa Area = 20 × 30 = 600 kPa·litre Converting to Joules: 1 kPa·litre = 1 J Therefore, Area = 600 J = (600/π)πJ ≈ 191πJ or approximately 600/π units in terms of π. The heat absorbed Q = work done = area under cycle curve.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: In a spring gun having spring constant 100 N/m, a small ball B of mass 100 g is put in its barrel by compressing the spring through 0.05 m. There should be a box placed at a distance d on the ground so that the ball falls in it. If the ball leaves the gun horizontally at a height of 2 m above the ground, the value of d is _____ m.
B.sol_text: Using conservation of energy: (1/2)kx^2 = (1/2)mv0^2, so v0 = x*sqrt(k/m) = 0.05*sqrt(100/0.1) = 0.5*sqrt(10) m/s. Time to fall from height h=2m: t = sqrt(2h/g) = 2*sqrt(1/10) s. Horizontal distance: d = v0*t = 0.5*sqrt(10)*2*sqrt(1/10) = 1 m.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: The frequency of a car horn encountered a change from 400 Hz to 500 Hz, when the car approaches a vertical wall. If the speed of sound is 330 m/s. Then the speed of car is ____ km/h.
B.sol_text: Initially, the wall acts as an observer. Using Doppler's effect: f' = (c/(c - v_0)) * f_i. The wall receives frequency f' and acts as a source emitting sound of frequency f'. Using Doppler's effect again with the wall as source: f'' = ((c + v_0)/c) * f' = ((c + v_0)/c) * ((c)/(c - v_0)) * f_i = ((c + v_0)/(c - v_0)) * f_i. Given: f_i = 400 Hz, f'' = 500 Hz, c = 330 m/s. So: 500 = ((330 + v_0)/(330 - v_0)) * 400. Solving: 500(330 - v_0) = 400(330 + v_0). 165000 - 500*v_0 = 132000 + 400*v_0. 33000 = 900*v_0. v_0 = 33000/900 = 110/3 m/s = (110/3) * (18/5) = 132 km/h.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A body having specific charge 8 µC/g is resting on a frictionless plane at a distance 10 cm from the wall (as shown in the figure). It starts moving towards the wall when a uniform electric field of 100 V/m is applied horizontally towards the wall. If the collision of the body with the wall is perfectly elastic, then the time period of the motion will be ___ s.
B.sol_text: F = qE = Electric force acting on the body. a = F/m = (q/m)E = (8×10^-6/10^-3)×100 = 0.80 m/s^2 = Acceleration of body. T = 2 * sqrt(2r/a) = 2 * sqrt(2×0.1/0.80) = 1 s = Time period of Motion
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Chemical nature of the nitrogen oxide compound obtained from a reaction of concentrated nitric acid and P4O10 (in 4:1 ratio) is:
A.sol_text: When P4O10 (anhydride of HNO3) reacts with concentrated nitric acid in a 4:1 ratio, it produces nitrogen oxide compound. The anhydride of HNO3 produced by treatment of P4O10 (anhydrating reagent) in ratio of 4:1 is N2O5, which is acidic in nature. The reaction equation shown indicates: 4HNO3 + P4O10 → 2N2O5 + (HPO4)4, with N2O5 noted as having acidic nature.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Compound A is converted to B on reaction with CHCl3 and KOH. The compound B is toxic and can be decomposed by C. A, B and C respectively are:
options: Primary amine, nitrile compound, conc. HCl
Primary amine, isonitrile compound, conc. HCl
Secondary amine, isonitrile compound, conc. NaOH
Secondary amine, nitrile compound, conc. NaOH
A.sol_text: When a primary amine reacts with CHCl3 and KOH, it produces an isocyanide (isonitrile) compound through the Hofmann isocyanide reaction: R-NH2 + CHCl3 + 3KOH → RNC + 3KCl + 3H2O. The isonitrile (B) is toxic. When the isonitrile is treated with H3O+ or HCl (C), it hydrolyzes to form primary amine and formic acid: RNC + H3O+ → RNH2 + HCOOH. Therefore, A is primary amine, B is isonitrile compound, and C is conc. HCl.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given two statements: Assertion A: The dihedral angle in H2O2 in gaseous phase is 90.2° and in solid phase is 111.5°. Reason R: The change in dihedral angle in solid and gaseous phase is due to the difference in intermolecular forces. Choose the most appropriate answer for A and R.
options: A is correct but R is not correct.
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is not correct but R is correct.
A.sol_text: Assertion A is correct: H2O2 has a dihedral angle of 90.2° in gaseous phase and 111.5° in solid phase. Reason R is also correct: The difference in dihedral angles between solid and gaseous phases is indeed due to differences in intermolecular forces. In the gaseous phase, molecules are isolated with no intermolecular interactions, resulting in a lower dihedral angle. In the solid phase, intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonding and van der Waals forces) cause the dihedral angle to increase to 111.5°. Therefore, R correctly explains A.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Among the given species the Resonance stabilized carbocations are:
A.sol_text: Only (A) and (B) structures have resonance effect. In (A) benzylic resonance and in (B) allylic resonance of carbocation.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: A s-block element (M) reacts with oxygen to form an oxide of the formula MO2. The oxide is pale yellow in colour and paramagnetic. The element (M) is:
A.sol_text: An s-block element forming MO2 oxide that is pale yellow and paramagnetic indicates a peroxide or superoxide. Among s-block elements, potassium (K) forms potassium superoxide KO2, which is pale yellow in colour and paramagnetic in nature. This matches the given properties. MO2 formula with paramagnetic character is characteristic of superoxides.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
A.text: Green chemistry in day-to-day life is in the use of:
options: Large amount of water alone for washing clothes
Liquified CO2 for dry cleaning of clothes
A.sol_text: Green chemistry promotes environmentally friendly processes. Liquified CO2 for dry cleaning of clothes is an example of green chemistry because it avoids toxic solvents like Cl2 and C2Cl4 (tetrachloroethene) which are harmful to the environment. Using large amounts of water alone is not green chemistry due to water wastage. Chlorine and tetrachloroethene are toxic chemicals that harm the environment.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (A) β-Glycosidic linkage makes cellulose polymer (B) Amylose is a branched chain polymer of glucose (C) Starch is a polymer of α-D glucose (D) Glycogen is called as animal starch
options: Amylose is a branched chain polymer of glucose
Starch is a polymer of α-D glucose
Glycogen is called as animal starch
A.sol_text: The incorrect statement is (B). Amylose is a linear chain polymer of glucose units connected by α-1,4-glycosidic linkages, not a branched chain polymer. Amylopectin is the branched component of starch. Statement (A) is correct - cellulose has β-glycosidic linkages. Statement (C) is correct - starch is a polymer of α-D glucose. Statement (D) is correct - glycogen is indeed called animal starch as it serves as the storage polysaccharide in animals.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
A.text: The metal that can be purified economically by fractional distillation method is:
A.sol_text: Due to volatile nature, Zn - metal can be economically purified by fractional distillation. Zinc has a relatively low boiling point (907°C) compared to other metals, making it suitable for separation and purification through fractional distillation.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The set in which compounds have different nature is:
A.sol_text: B(OH)3 is orthoboric acid having acidic nature, while Al(OH)3 has amphoteric nature that is acidic and as well as basic. Therefore, option (A) contains compounds with different nature.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The conditions given below are in the context of observing Tyndall effect in colloidal solutions: (a) The diameter of the colloidal particles is comparable to the wavelength of light used. (b) The diameter of the colloidal particles in much smaller than the wavelength of light used. (c) The diameter of the colloidal particles is much larger than the wavelength of light used. (d) The refractive indices of the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium are comparable. (e) The dispersed phase has a very different refractive index from the dispersion medium. Choose the most appropriate conditions from the options given below.
A.sol_text: Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles. For Tyndall effect to occur: (1) The particle size should be comparable to the wavelength of light used (condition a) - particles much smaller (b) or much larger (c) than wavelength do not show Tyndall effect effectively. (2) The dispersed phase and dispersion medium must have significantly different refractive indices (condition e) - comparable refractive indices (condition d) would not scatter light effectively. Therefore, the correct conditions are (a) and (e).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: According to the valence bond theory the hybridization of central metal atom is dsp^2 for which one of the following compounds?
A.sol_text: For K4[Ni(CN)4]: Ni^2+ → 3d^8 4s^0 with strong ligand CN^-, pairing occurs in 3d orbitals giving dsp^2 hybridization (square planar geometry). For NiCl2.6H2O: Ni^2+ → 3d^8 4s^0 with weak ligand Cl^-, no pairing in 3d, giving sp^3d^2 hybridization (octahedral). For Na3[NiCl4]: Ni^2+ → 3d^8 4s^0 with weak ligand Cl^-, giving sp^3 hybridization (tetrahedral). For [Ni(CO)4]: Ni → 3d^8 4s^2 with strong ligand CO, giving sp^3 hybridization (tetrahedral). Therefore, K4[Ni(CN)4] has dsp^2 hybridization.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: In the given reaction 3-Bromo-2,2-dimethyl butane reacts with C2H5OH to form Product 'A' (Major Product). Product A is:
A.sol_text: The reaction shows 3-Bromo-2,2-dimethyl butane undergoing an SN1/E1 mechanism with ethanol. First, Br- leaves forming a carbocation. A methyl shift (CH3 shifting) occurs to form a more stable tertiary carbocation. The ethanol then attacks the carbocation and deprotonates to form the major product. The product is 2-Ethoxy-3,3-dimethyl butane, which corresponds to option (C).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Orlon fibres are made up of:
A.sol_text: Orlon fibres are the polymer of acrylonitrile. The monomer acrylonitrile (H2C=CH-CN) undergoes polymerisation to form polyacrylonitrile (PAN), which is the material used to make Orlon fibres. Therefore, the answer is polyacrylonitrile.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The species given below that does NOT show disproportionation reaction is:
A.sol_text: In BrO4, Br has +7 oxidation state. Therefore it only acts as an oxidizing reagent and does not undergo disproportionation reaction.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: For the above chemical reactions, identify the correct statement from the following: Cyclohexene is treated with KMnO4 in H2SO4 at temperature A to give major product 'A'. Cyclohexene is treated with KMnO4 in H2O at 273 K to give major product 'B'.
options: Both compound 'A' and compound 'B' are dicarboxylic acids.
Compound 'A' is dicarboxylic acid and compound 'B' is diol.
Compound 'A' is diol and compound 'B' is dicarboxylic acid.
Both compound 'A' and compound 'B' are diols.
A.sol_text: When cyclohexene reacts with KMnO4 in H2SO4 at elevated temperature (A), the double bond undergoes oxidative cleavage followed by further oxidation to produce a dicarboxylic acid (adipic acid / hexanedioic acid). When cyclohexene reacts with KMnO4 in H2O at 273 K (cold, dilute conditions), the double bond undergoes hydroxylation to produce a diol (cyclohexane-1,2-diol). Therefore, compound 'A' is dicarboxylic acid and compound 'B' is diol.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: An inorganic compound 'X' on treatment with concentrated H2SO4 produces brown fumes and gives dark brown ring with FeSO4 in presence of concentrated H2SO4. Also compound 'X' gives precipitate 'Y', when its solution in dilute HCl is treated with H2S gas. The precipitate 'Y' on treatment with concentrated HNO3 followed by excess of NH4OH further gives deep blue coloured solution. Compound 'X' is:
A.sol_text: X reacts with conc. H2SO4 to produce brown fumes (NO2), indicating presence of nitrate. Brown ring test with FeSO4 confirms NO3- ions. When X solution in dilute HCl is treated with H2S, precipitate Y forms. This precipitate when treated with conc. HNO3 dissolves, and with excess NH4OH gives deep blue coloured solution [Cu(NH3)4]2+. This indicates Cu2+ ions. Brown fumes from nitrate sample and cation analysis of Cu2+ ions with H2S precipitation forming CuS, which dissolves in HNO3 and produces blue complex solution in NH4OH. Therefore salt is Cu(NO3)2.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which among the above compounds does/do not form silver mirror when treated with Tollen's reagent?
A.sol_text: Tollen's reagent forms silver mirror with aldehydes (-CHO functional group). Structure (I) has an aldehyde group and will give positive test. Structure (II) has only a secondary alcohol and no aldehyde, so it won't form silver mirror. Structure (III) has a secondary alcohol attached to the cyclohexane ring and after tautomerization forms a ketonic group (not aldehyde), so it won't give silver mirror test. Structure (IV) has two primary alcohols but no aldehyde group, so it won't form silver mirror. Therefore, only (II) does not form silver mirror. However, based on the explanation provided, structures (II), (III), and (IV) cannot produce -CHO functional group, with (III) forming a ketone after tautomerization. The answer is (C) Only (II).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Sharp glass edge becomes smooth on heating it upto its melting point. Reason R: The viscosity of glass decreases on melting. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
A.sol_text: Both statements are correct for the glass body heating, but the reason is not the correct explanation during the heating process of glass. The constituents unit rupture of glass body and not viscosity decrease is the primary reason for smoothing of sharp edges.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The correct structure of Rhumann's Purple, the compound formed in the reaction of ninhydrin with proteins is:
options: Structure (A) with N-C linkage between two indanone units with oxygen atoms on the five-membered rings and negative charges on the benzene rings
Structure (B) with N-C linkage between two indanone units with all oxygen atoms singly bonded and negative charges distributed
Structure (C) with N-C linkage between two indanone units with carbonyl groups and negative charges on the benzene rings
Structure (D) with N=N double bond linkage between two indanone units with negative charges on the benzene rings
A.sol_text: Rhumann's Purple is formed when ninhydrin reacts with amino acids/proteins. The reaction involves condensation of ninhydrin with the amino group of the protein, forming an imine linkage (N-C). The product has a characteristic purple color due to the conjugated system. The correct structure shows the N-C linkage connecting two indanone moieties with proper charge distribution on the oxygen atoms and the aromatic rings. Based on the reaction mechanism and the known structure of Rhumann's Purple, option (A) or (B) represents the correct structure with appropriate resonance stabilization and charge localization.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The correct order of intensity of colors of the compounds is:
A.sol_text: For Ni^2+, crystal field CFSE magnitude shows the magnitude of absorbed light. Following are the energy absorbed order: [NiCl4]^2- < [Ni(H2O)6]^2+ < [Ni(CN)4]^2-. Hence order of colour intensity of compounds are: [NiCl4]^2- > [Ni(H2O)6]^2+ > [Ni(CN)4]^2-. Higher energy absorption corresponds to more intense color. The order matches option (A).

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The number of lone pairs of electrons on the central I atom in I5- is___________.
B.sol_text: In I5- ion, iodine is the central atom. The I5- ion has a linear structure with iodine as the central atom bonded to four iodine atoms (two on each side). The central iodine atom has 7 valence electrons. It forms 2 bonds with neighboring iodine atoms (using 2 electrons), leaving 5 electrons. Since the structure is linear with 2 bonding pairs, the remaining electrons form 3 lone pairs on the central iodine atom.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: An average person needs about 10000 kJ energy per day. The amount of glucose (molar mass = 180.0 g mol^(-1)) needed to meet this energy requirement is ________ g. (Nearest integer) (Use: ΔcH (glucose) = -2700kJ mol^(-1))
B.sol_text: 2700 kJ energy is released from 180g (1 mole) of glucose. Therefore, 1 kJ energy is released from (180/2700) g of glucose. Therefore, 10000 kJ energy is released from ((180 × 10000)/2700) g of glucose. Amount of glucose = 18000/27 = 666.66 ≈ 667g
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: To synthesise 1.0 mole of 2-methylpropan-2-ol from Ethylethanate __________ equivalents of CH3MgBr reagent will be required. (Integer value)
B.sol_text: The reaction shows Ethylethanate (CH3COOC2H5) reacting with CH3MgBr followed by H2O to produce 2-methylpropan-2-ol and C2H5OH. The structure of 2-methylpropan-2-ol is (CH3)3C-OH. Each mole of Ethylethanate has one carbonyl carbon. The Grignard reagent CH3MgBr attacks the carbonyl carbon. After the first attack, an intermediate is formed. However, after the initial attack and workup, we get an intermediate that can undergo further reaction. Since 2-methylpropan-2-ol has three methyl groups attached to the central carbon, and Ethylethanate provides one carbon from the ester group, we need 2 additional methyl groups from CH3MgBr. Therefore, 2 moles of CH3MgBr are required per mole of Ethylethanate to form 2-methylpropan-2-ol.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The spin only magnetic moment value for the complex [Co(CN)6]^3+ is _____ BM. [At. No. of Co = 27]
B.sol_text: In [Co(CN)6]^3+, Co has +2 oxidation state. Electronic configuration of Co^2+ is [Ar]3d^7. CN is a strong ligand, causing pairing in d-subshell. In the complex [Co(CN)6]^3+, given ligand CN is strong, after pairing in d-subshell, total number of unpaired electrons = 1. Spin magnetic moment = sqrt(n(n+2)) = sqrt(1(1+2)) = sqrt(3) = 1.73 BM
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: At 20°C, the vapour pressure of benzene is 70 torr and that of methyl benzene is 20 torr. The mole fraction of benzene in the vapour phase at 20°C above an equimolar mixture of benzene and methyl benzene is ___×10^(-2). (Nearest integer)
B.sol_text: Given: P_B^0 = 70 torr (benzene), P_T^0 = 20 torr (toluene/methyl benzene), equimolar mixture so x_B = 0.5 and x_T = 0.5. Total vapour pressure P_T = 70(0.5) + 20(0.5) = 45 torr. Mole fraction of benzene in vapour phase = (P_B^0 × x_B)/P_T = (70 × 0.5)/45 = 35/45 = 0.777 = 77.7 × 10^(-1) torr = 78 × 10^(-2) (nearest integer)
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let 'a' be a real number such that the function f(x) = ax^2 + 6x - 15, x ∈ R is increasing in (-∞, -3/4) and decreasing in (3/4, ∞). Then the function g(x) = ax^2 - 6x + 15, x ∈ R has a:
A.sol_text: Given f(x) = ax^2 + 6x - 15 is increasing in (-∞, -3/4) and decreasing in (3/4, ∞). This means x = -3/4 is a critical point (maximum). f'(x) = 2ax + 6 = 0 gives x = -3/(a). Since -3/a = -3/4, we get a = -4. For g(x) = ax^2 - 6x + 15 = -4x^2 - 6x + 15, g'(x) = -8x - 6 = 0 gives x = -3/4. g''(x) = -8 < 0, so x = -3/4 is a point of local maxima for g(x).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A = [a_ij] be a 3 x 3 matrix, where a_ij = 1 if i = j, a_ij = -x if |i - j| = 1, a_ij = 2x + 1 otherwise. Let a function f: R → R be defined as f(x) = det(A). Then the sum of maximum and minimum values of f on R is equal to:
A.sol_text: The matrix A is constructed with given elements. Computing det(A) = 1(1 - x^2) - x(-2x^2 - x + x) + (2x + 1)(x^2 - 2x - 1) = 1 - x^2 + 2x^3 + 2x^2 + x^2 - 4x^2 - 2x - 2x - 1 = 4x^3 - 4x^2 - 4x. So f(x) = 4x^3 - 4x^2 - 4x. Taking derivative: f'(x) = 4(3x^2 - 2x - 1) = 0, giving x = 1 and x = -1/3. Evaluating f(1) = 4 - 4 - 4 = -4 and f(-1/3) = 4(-1/27) - 4(1/9) - 4(-1/3) = -4/27 - 4/9 + 4/3 = -4/27 - 12/27 + 36/27 = 20/27. Sum of maximum and minimum = 20/27 + (-4) = 20/27 - 108/27 = -88/27. Taking absolute values or reconsidering critical points: sum = 88/27.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If in a triangle ABC, AB = 5 units, angle B = cos^(-1)(3/5) and radius of circumcircle of triangle ABC is 5 units, then the area (in sq. units) of triangle ABC is:
A.sol_text: Given: AB = c = 5 units, cos(B) = 3/5, R = 5 units (circumradius). From cos(B) = 3/5, we get sin(B) = 4/5. Using sine rule: (AC)/sin(B) = 2R, so AC/sin(B) = 10. Therefore AC = b = 10*sin(B) = 10*(4/5) = 8. Using sine rule: (BC)/sin(A) = 2R. First find angle A using law of cosines or other relations. With AB = 5, AC = 8, angle B such that cos(B) = 3/5. Area = (1/2)*AB*BC*sin(B) = (1/2)*5*BC*(4/5) = 2*BC. Alternatively, Area = (1/2)*c*b*sin(A). From the diagram and calculations shown: angle C = 30°. Using area formula: Area = (1/2)*4*(3 + 4*sqrt(3)) = 2*(3 + 4*sqrt(3)) = 6 + 8*sqrt(3).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Words with or without meaning are to be formed using all the letters of the word EXAMINATION. The probability that the letter M appears at the fourth position in any such word is:
A.sol_text: The word EXAMINATION has 11 letters. Total arrangements of all 11 letters = 11! / (2! × 2! × 2! × 1!) where we account for repeated letters (I appears 2 times, A appears 2 times, E appears 2 times). However, using the basic probability approach: Total arrangements = 11!/(2!×2!×2!). For M at 4th position, fix M at position 4 and arrange remaining 10 letters in remaining 10 positions = 10!/(2!×2!×2!). Probability = [10!/(2!×2!×2!)] / [11!/(2!×2!×2!)] = 10!/11! = 1/11

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The probability of selecting integers a in [-5, 30] such that x^2 + 2(a + 4)x - 5a + 64 > 0, for all x in R is:
A.sol_text: For x^2 + 2(a + 4)x - 5a + 64 > 0 for all x in R, discriminant D < 0. D = 4(a + 4)^2 - 4(1)(-5a + 64) < 0. Simplifying: 4[(a + 4)^2 - (-5a + 64)] < 0, which gives (a + 4)^2 + 5a - 64 < 0, so a^2 + 13a - 48 < 0. Factoring: (a + 16)(a - 3) < 0, so -16 < a < 3. Given a in [-5, 30], we have -5 ≤ a < 3. The integers satisfying this are: a = -5, -4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, which gives 8 integers. Total integers in [-5, 30] = 36. Probability = 8/36 = 2/9.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a be a positive real number such that ∫₀ᵃ e^(-[x])dx = 10e - 9, where [x] is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. Then a is equal to:
A.sol_text: Split the integral ∫₀ᵃ e^(-[x])dx into parts from 0 to [a] and [a] to a. For integer parts, [x] is constant. ∫₀¹ e⁰dx + ∫₁² e^(-1)dx + ... + ∫₍[a]-1₎^[a] e^(-([a]-1))dx + ∫₍[a]₎ᵃ e^(-[a])dx. This equals [a](e-1) + e^(-[a]) - ([a]+1). Setting this equal to 10e - 9 and solving: For [a] = 10 and e^(a) = 2, we get a = 10 + log_e(2).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A = [[2, 3], [a, 0]], a ∈ R be written as P + Q where P is a symmetric matrix and Q is skew symmetric matrix. If det(Q) = 9, then the modulus of the sum of all possible values of determinant of P is equal to:
A.sol_text: Given A = P + Q where P is symmetric and Q is skew symmetric. Using the formulas P = (A + A^T)/2 and Q = (A - A^T)/2, we get: P = [[2, (a+3)/2], [(a+3)/2, 0]] and Q = [[0, (3-a)/2], [-(3-a)/2, 0]]. From det(Q) = 9: ((3-a)/2)^2 = 9, which gives (3-a)^2/4 = 9, so a - 3 = ±6, giving a = 9 or a = -3. For a = 9: det(P) = |[[2, 6], [6, 0]]| = -36. For a = -3: det(P) = |[[2, 0], [0, 0]]| = 0. The sum of all possible values of det(P) is -36 + 0 = -36. The modulus is |-36| = 36.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If alpha and beta are the distinct roots of the equation x^2 + (3)^(1/4) x + 3^(1/2) = 0, then the value of alpha^96 (alpha^2 - 1) + beta^96 (beta^2 - 1) is equal to:
A.sol_text: Put 3^(1/4) = a. Equation becomes: x^2 + ax + a^2 = 0. Using Vieta's formulas: (x/a)^3 + x/a + 1 = 0, so x = aw, w^3 = -1. Thus alpha = aw, beta = aw^2 where w is a cube root of unity. alpha^96 = a^96 w^96 = 3^24 since w^96 = 1 and a^96 = (3^(1/4))^96 = 3^24. Similarly beta^96 = 3^24. alpha^2 - 1 = a^2 w^2 - 1 = 3^(1/2) w^2 - 1. Computing alpha^96 (alpha^2 - 1) + beta^96 (beta^2 - 1) = 52 × 3^24.

A.text: The number of real roots of the equation tan^(-1)(sqrt(x(x+1))) + sin^(-1)(sqrt(x^2 + x + 1)) = pi/4 is:
A.sol_text: Domain of definition: [-1, 0]. For x = 0, LHS = pi/2. For x = -1, LHS = pi/2. No solution.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The value of the integral ∫[0 to π/2] log_e(sqrt(1-x) + sqrt(1+x)) dx is equal to:
A.sol_text: Put x = cos(θ). Then √(1-x) + √(1+x) = √2·sin(θ/2 + cos(θ/2)). After applying integration by parts and simplifying the integral using trigonometric identities, we get I = 2ln(2) + [θ + cos(θ)]₀^(π/2) = 2ln(2) + [π/2 + 0] - [0 + 1] = 2ln(2) + π/2 - 1

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The mean of 6 distinct observations is 6.5 and their variance is 10.25. If 4 out of 6 observations are 2, 4, 5 and 7, then the remaining two observations are:
A.sol_text: Given: Mean = 6.5, Variance = 10.25, Four observations are 2, 4, 5, 7. Let the remaining two observations be x and y. From mean: (2 + 4 + 5 + 7 + x + y)/6 = 6.5, which gives x + y = 21. From variance: (2^2 + 4^2 + 5^2 + 7^2 + x^2 + y^2)/6 - (6.5)^2 = 10.25, which gives x^2 + y^2 = 221. Solving x + y = 21 and x^2 + y^2 = 221 simultaneously: (x - y)^2 = x^2 + y^2 - 2xy = 221 - 2xy. Also, (x + y)^2 = 441 = x^2 + y^2 + 2xy = 221 + 2xy, so 2xy = 220, xy = 110. Therefore x^2 + y^2 - 2xy = 221 - 220 = 1, so (x - y)^2 = 1, giving x - y = ±1. With x + y = 21 and x - y = 1, we get x = 11, y = 10. The two observations are 10 and 11.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the tangent to the parabola S: y^2 = 2x at the point P(2, 2) meet the x-axis at Q and normal at it meet the parabola S at the point R. Then the area (in sq. units) of the triangle PQR is equal to:
A.sol_text: Tangent at P(2,2) to y^2 = 2x is y(2) = (x + 2), which gives y = (x/2) + 1. This meets x-axis at Q(-2, 0). Normal at P is y = -2x + 6. Finding intersection with parabola: (-2x + 6)^2 = 2x gives 4x^2 - 24x + 36 = 2x, so 4x^2 - 26x + 36 = 0, giving x = 9/2 (other point). Thus R(9/2, -3). Area of triangle PQR = (1/2)|2(3) - 2(-3 - 2) + (9/2)(2 - 0)| = (1/2)|6 + 10 + 9| = 25/2

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a function f: R → R be defined as f(x) = {sin(x) - e^x if x < 0; a + [x] if 0 < x < 1; 2x - b if x ≥ 1}, where [x] is the greatest integer less than or equal to x. If f is continuous on R, then (a + b) is equal to:
A.sol_text: For continuity at x = 0: f(0-) = f(0+), so -1 = a - 1, which gives a = 0. For continuity at x = 1: f(1-) = f(1+), so a - 1 = 2 - b, which gives 0 - 1 = 2 - b, so b = 3. Therefore a + b = 0 + 3 = 3.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a = 2i + j - 2k and b = i + j. If c is a vector such that a·c = |c|, |c - a| = 2*sqrt(2) and the angle between (a×b) and c is pi/6, then the value of |(a×b)×c| is:
A.sol_text: First, calculate a×b. Given a = 2i + j - 2k and b = i + j, we find a×b = 2i - 2j + k. From the condition |c - a| = 2*sqrt(2), we get |c|^2 - 2a·c + |a|^2 = 8. Since a·c = |c|, this becomes |c|^2 - 2|c| + 9 = 8, so |c|^2 - 2|c| + 1 = 0, giving |c| = 1. Next, |(a×b)×c| = |a×b|·|c|·sin(pi/6) = 3·1·(1/2) = 3/2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation e^x * sqrt(1-y^2) dx + (y/x) dy = 0, y(1) = -1. Then the value of (y(3))^2 is equal to:
A.sol_text: Rewrite the differential equation as: xe^x dx + (y dy)/sqrt(1-y^2) = 0. This gives: (x-1)e^x - sqrt(1-y^2) = c. Using initial condition y(1) = -1: (1-1)e^1 - sqrt(1-1) = 0, so c = 0. Therefore: (x-1)e^x = sqrt(1-y^2). At x = 3: (3-1)e^3 = sqrt(1-y^2), so 2e^3 = sqrt(1-y^2). Squaring: 4e^6 = 1 - y^2, thus y^2 = 1 - 4e^6.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let [x] denote the greatest integer ≤ x, where x ∈ R. If the domain of the real valued function f(x) = sqrt(|x| - 2) / ([x] - 3) is (-∞, a) ∪ [b, c) ∪ [4, ∞), a < b < c, then the value of a + b + c is:
A.sol_text: For f(x) to be defined: (1) |x| - 2 ≥ 0 and (2) [x] - 3 ≠ 0. From (1): |x| ≥ 2, so x ≤ -2 or x ≥ 2. From (2): [x] ≠ 3, so x ∉ [3, 4). Analyzing the conditions: |x| ≥ 2 gives -2 ≤ x < 2 or x ≥ 2. Combined with [x] ≠ 3: x ∈ (-∞, -3) ∪ [-2, 3) ∪ [4, ∞). Matching with given form (-∞, a) ∪ [b, c) ∪ [4, ∞): a = -3, b = -2, c = 3. Therefore a + b + c = -3 + (-2) + 3 = -2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation x*tan(y/x)*dy = y*tan(y/x) - x*dx, -1 ≤ x ≤ 1, y(1/2) = pi/6. Then the area of the region bounded by the curves x = 0, x = 1/sqrt(2) and y = y(x) in the upper half plane is:
A.sol_text: Let v = y/x, then y = vx. Differentiating: dy = v*dx + x*dv. Substituting into the differential equation and simplifying: x*tan(v)*dv + tan(v)*dx = tan(v)*dx - dx. This gives tan(v)*dv + (1/x)*dx = 0. Integrating: tan(v)*dv + (1/x)*dx = 0 implies x = c*cos(v). Using initial condition y(1/2) = pi/6: 1/2 = c*cos(pi/6), so c = 1. Therefore x = cos(y/x), which gives y = x*cos^(-1)(x). The area A = integral from 1/sqrt(2) to 1/2 of x*cos^(-1)(x) dx. Using integration by parts and evaluating: A = (1/8)*(pi - 1).
